title: 肾脏拍卖案例：实证与规范问题
titleEn: Kidney Auction Case: Positive vs. Normative Questions

items.text: 有人以2.5万美元起拍在eBay拍卖肾脏，价格被炒至500万美元后才被eBay关闭；eBay禁止拍卖人体器官。
items.textEn: A kidney was auctioned on eBay starting at $25,000; bidding reached $5 million before eBay shut it down.

items.text: 实证问题：价格为何这么高？用供需模型解释：肾的需求极高（需要肾才能活的人会倾其所有），自由市场供给极低，故价格极高。
items.textEn: Positive question: why so high? High demand (people will pay everything to live) and very low supply produce a very high price.

sections.heading: 规范问题：器官该不该卖？
sections.headingEn: Normative Question: Should Organs Be Sold?

items.text: 规范问题：我们该不该被允许在eBay上出售器官？这本质是经济学问题，不是哲学问题。
items.textEn: Normative question: should we be allowed to sell organs? This is fundamentally an economics question, not philosophy.

items.text: 美国每年约5万人死于器官短缺，约10万人患丙肝（丙肝可导致肾衰竭）；富人愿买、穷人愿卖（一个肾也能正常生活，可改变家庭命运）。
items.textEn: ~50,000 Americans die yearly from organ shortage; ~100,000 live with hepatitis C, which causes kidney failure.

items.text: 老师强调：前11讲自由市场为王；经济学基本是右翼科学，只有两种理由可以干预市场，第一种是市场失灵。
items.textEn: For the first 11 lectures the free market is king; only two reasons justify interfering with markets—the first is market failure.

items.text: 人们可能不知情：丙肝可潜伏多年，卖肾后才发现患病则可能死亡；人们可能被强迫（如强迫子女捐肾）或卷入犯罪活动。
items.textEn: People may be misinformed (hepatitis C can lie dormant for years) or coerced (e.g., forcing children to donate).

items.text: 重点：黑市本身不算市场失灵的理由——经济学家认为黑市也是市场，若无其他失灵，黑市交易也可以。
items.textEn: Key point: the black market is NOT a market failure—economists treat it as a market; without other failures it's acceptable.
